# clihelp

> A declarative Go library for command-line applications: hierarchical command
> routing, pflag-backed option binding, and width-aware coloured help, manual
> pages and Markdown generated from one struct literal.

Import path: `github.com/sarielhp/clihelp`

This file follows the llms.txt convention: it is an index, not a specification.
It used to be a copy of the API, and a copy drifts — it named three functions
that no longer existed and told readers to call a method as a package function,
which produced code that did not compile. The authoritative API is `go doc
github.com/sarielhp/clihelp`, which cannot drift because it is generated from
the source.

## Start here

- [How clihelp decides](docs/how-clihelp-decides.md): the mechanism. The eleven decisions the library makes on the author's behalf, what each reads from `App`, `Command` and `Option`, what it assumes when a field is undeclared, and what is lost by leaving it so. Then the invariants a caller can rely on, the things the library already does so that nobody builds them twice, the escape hatches and their cost, and a complete annotated application.

## Reference

- [Execution lifecycle and routing](docs/lifecycle-and-routing.md): pipeline order, lifecycle hooks, abort semantics, `Context`, subcommands.
- [Flag and option specification](docs/flags-and-options.md): the spec-string syntax (`"--tag <v>, -t, -T"`), the constructors, toggle pairs, custom value types, and the reserved help flags.
- [Shell integration](docs/completion.md): one-command setup and the files it writes, the Alt-H binding, manual pages, the reserved `__clihelp` verbs, and the generators a packager uses.
- [Markdown generation](docs/markdown-generation.md): generating a help tree, and the hash that keeps it current.
- [Recipes and patterns](docs/recipes-and-patterns.md): cancellation, testing commands with `clihelptest`, dynamic completion, theming.

## Optional

- [Comparison with spf13/cobra](docs/comparison-with-cobra.md): differences and the reasoning behind them.
- [Changelog](CHANGES.md): every behaviour change, with the defect that motivated it.
